The record held it only in pieces: [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) for individuation, [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) for function, [CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) for viability. Filed in will-organization, where the question of what organizes an agent's standards sits and where [CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) marks the limit, rather than pragmatic-transport, which holds the transport of judgments between contexts ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), [QUESTION-130](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-130.md)) and not their indexing. The sharp edge: it is the constitutive half only. That the standards themselves can be objectively better or worse is not claimed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-364](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-364.md) v2 | Low supervisory cost cannot show non-domination: processes conditioned never to object also coordinate without override, so whether an organization dominates its processes must be read from what happens when a constituent dissents, and from its history | A45's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against the owner's non-domination criterion ([CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md)) read through its economy: "a system whose subordinate processes have been conditioned never to object might exhibit perfect local harmony", and "A quiet subordinate process isn't necessarily a satisfied one." It is [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md)'s manipulation objection, and [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md), applied to the new criterion. It does not say the criterion fails, only that cost cannot certify it. The authenticity line was set aside on 2026-10-05; whether it reopens is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) v2 | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either | The owner's, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe we should focus less on distress and more on frustration". A33 granted it: "Frustration is the most promising theoretical primitive of the three." Frustration is a fact about demands, admissible transformations and governance, so it can be stated without feelings and without a common scale. It supersedes in substance the distress-first formulations of A28–A32, which were never filed. The sharp edge: it says what to start from, not that a frustrated organization is distressed or feels anything. The claim bears on the organizational-affect line, which is Deferred ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md)); whether that line reopens is the owner's decision, not made here. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-399](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "We should not present governance-preserving coarse-graining as a new general theory of causal abstraction." That stands. But it is not an instance of these papers' notions either: their criteria compare interventional laws and let the high-level context be any map that works, so they accept the hidden governance bit, whose coarse state keeps nothing of the response to h. Re-checked step by step against the three THEORYs. It corrects [TERM-067](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md)'s first wording, which read the profile as [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md)'s causal component with the identity correspondence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md) v2 | A coarse-graining exactly informationally closed under a process's ordinary dynamics need not preserve its responses to an intervention on the mechanism: for a declared intervention distribution ρ, independent of the state, the deficiency Γ = I(S; Y^(I) \| T(S), I) can be positive, as in the hidden governance bit, where it is ρ(h = 1) bits; and Γ = 0 exactly when, for every intervention ρ charges, the response kernels are constant on T's fibres over the states of positive probability | A16 §3–4 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 and A17 §4.2–4.3, its paper's Proposition 1, reused at A18 and in A23's audit. A16: "a representation can be perfectly informationally closed under the ordinary dynamics while failing to preserve a governance-relevant counterfactual distinction." The witness is [CASE-125](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-125.md); the proof is in the body, checked exactly on 2026-10-21. The qualitative point was on file: [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md)'s "What it does not say" (A22's Construction B of 2026-10-17, [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md)), and [CLAIM-122](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md)'s supervisory test, whose note of 2026-10-18 has it without parameters. New here are the parameters, the deficiency Γ and the exact condition for Γ = 0. It is an application of ordinary causal sufficiency, not new information theory, and it does not say the system governs itself. | Active |
| [CLAIM-410](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md) v2 | Removing a constraint on an organization's members does not move it along one scale of more or less governance: it changes a profile of who holds rule-making, monitoring, enforcement, appeal and revision, in which the authority the constraint held can be eliminated, distributed or transferred, and the members' first-order options and their share in revising the conditions of their action can move in opposite directions | The owner's question, U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what does this suggest about e.g. "deregulation" as an ideological end?" A18: removing a regulator "does not remove governance", and the question is whether a change "eliminate[s] an exercise of authority, distribute[s] that authority, or transfer[s] it to another locus". Its five-part profile generalizes [TERM-017](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-017.md)'s three relations, which "can vary independently" ([CLAIM-057](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-057.md)), and its two freedoms are [CLAIM-086](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-086.md)'s distinction carried from a constraint to its removal. The sharp edge: it says nothing about whether any deregulation is good, or about what any actual reform did. A18: "This doesn't establish that deregulation is good or bad." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-422](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-422.md) v2 | A successful corrective act, an executable procedure and a maintained organizational capacity are three different things, so an organization can record a correction, even rewrite its rules, without the corrected capacity being maintained | From A24 and A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, on the owner's cases of a fireground mayday that changed a safety culture (U23) and NASA's learning before and after Challenger (U25). A24: "A successful act, an executable procedure, and a maintained organizational capacity are three different things." A25: "Institutional learning is not complete when an organization changes its rules." It rests on [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md), which separates the operative regime, the governing organization and the capacity to transform it, and grounds in the record's reading of the Columbia board ([THEORY-140](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md)). The edge: a recorded correction is evidence of a correction, not of its maintenance. | Proposed |
